mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a veneer to suddenly feel rough?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not unusual for veneers to feel slightly different over time, but a sudden rough sensation — particularly one where the tongue consistently catches on an edge — is worth having assessed. This type of change can indicate chipping, surface wear, or a shift in the veneer's bond. A dentist can examine the area, identify the cause, and discuss suitable next steps. Do not assume the issue will resolve itself, as early assessment generally allows more straightforward management options to be considered.

mainEntity.name: Can I continue eating and drinking normally if my veneer has a rough edge?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, you can continue with your normal diet while awaiting a dental appointment, but it is sensible to avoid very hard, crunchy, or sticky foods that might place additional stress on the affected veneer. This may help prevent the situation from worsening before you are seen by a dentist. If you experience pain, significant sensitivity, or the veneer appears to have moved or loosened, contact your dental practice sooner rather than waiting.

mainEntity.name: How long do veneers typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of dental veneers varies depending on the material used, the individual patient's dental habits, and how well they are maintained. Porcelain veneers may last anywhere from ten to fifteen years or more with appropriate care, whilst composite resin veneers tend to require more frequent maintenance or replacement. Regular dental reviews and good oral hygiene practices are important factors in how long veneers remain in good condition. Your dentist can advise you on the expected longevity based on your specific veneers.

mainEntity.name: Could a veneer catching my tongue damage my gums?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a veneer has a sharp or rough edge, it may cause minor irritation to the surrounding gum tissue or inner cheek over time. In most cases this is not severe, but persistent irritation to soft tissues is worth addressing. If you notice gum redness, swelling, or soreness around the veneer, this is an additional reason to book a dental review. Your dentist can assess the gum tissue alongside the veneer itself and advise on appropriate management.

mainEntity.name: Will I need a new veneer if the edge is rough?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Whether a veneer requires replacement depends on the nature and extent of the problem identified during clinical examination. Minor surface irregularities may be resolved through polishing or composite repair. However, if the veneer is significantly damaged, debonded, or no longer fitting correctly, replacement may be the most appropriate option. Your dentist will discuss all clinically suitable options with you following a thorough assessment, ensuring any decision is based on your individual dental health needs.

mainEntity.name: Does a veneer catching the tongue mean the veneer is failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. A rough or catching sensation can have various causes, not all of which indicate complete veneer failure. In some cases, it may be a minor issue that can be addressed relatively easily. However, it is important not to dismiss the sensation, as changes in how a veneer feels can sometimes be an early indicator of a developing issue with the bond or structure. Seeking a professional assessment allows your dentist to determine the actual cause and advise you accordingly.
